name: One-arm pull-up
goal: 1 strict one-arm pull-up on each arm

stages.name: Pull-up base
stages.work: Strict pull-ups, scapular pulls, dead hangs, short one-arm hangs

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
exercises.cue: Arms straight. Pull the shoulder blades down; the elbows do not bend.

exercises.name: Strict pull-up
exercises.cue: Overhand, chin clearly over the bar, full lockout at the bottom.

exercises.name: Dead hang
exercises.cue: Active shoulders, relaxed grip pressure.

exercises.name: One-arm hang
exercises.cue: The other hand takes some weight (on the wrist or a band) if the shoulder complains. Stop at any elbow pain.

stages.name: Weighted
stages.work: Weighted pull-ups ramping to +25 % bodyweight (uses your bodyweight rule)

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
exercises.cue: Arms straight. Pull the shoulder blades down; the elbows do not bend.

exercises.name: Weighted pull-up, warm-up
exercises.cue: Easy and smooth. Hang fully at the bottom.

exercises.name: Weighted pull-up, working sets
exercises.cue: Chin clearly over the bar, no swing, full hang at the bottom.
exercises.note: Add reps first. When all three sets reach 5 clean reps, re-test your 5RM and the weight follows. Leave a rep in reserve on every set.

exercises.name: Weighted pull-up, +25 % bodyweight
exercises.cue: Same strict reps as the working sets, with the weight hanging still.
exercises.note: This is the stage standard. Try it only when the working sets feel easy, and no more than once every two weeks. Stop at any elbow pain.

exercises.name: One-arm hang
exercises.cue: The other hand takes some weight (on the wrist or a band) if the shoulder complains. Stop at any elbow pain.

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
exercises.cue: Arms straight. Pull the shoulder blades down; the elbows do not bend.

exercises.name: Wide-grip pull-up
exercises.cue: Hands wider than the shoulders, elbows out to the sides, chin over the bar.
exercises.note: Move the hands a little wider each week while the shoulders feel fine.

exercises.name: Archer pull-up
exercises.cue: Pull toward one hand. The other arm stays straight and just slides along the bar.
exercises.note: Start with the helping arm bent a little. Work toward a fully straight helping arm by the end of the stage. Keep that elbow soft, never snapped straight. Stop at any elbow pain.

exercises.name: One-arm hang
exercises.cue: The other hand takes some weight (on the wrist or a band) if the shoulder complains. Stop at any elbow pain.

stages.name: Assisted one-arm
stages.work: One-arm with the other hand on the wrist or a towel/band, assist reducing

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
exercises.cue: Arms straight. Pull the shoulder blades down; the elbows do not bend.

exercises.name: Archer pull-up
exercises.cue: Pull toward one hand. The other arm stays straight and just slides along the bar.
exercises.note: This is a warm-up for the one-arm work. Skip it on any day the elbow feels warm or sore.

exercises.name: Assisted one-arm pull-up
exercises.cue: Pull with one arm. The other hand holds the working wrist and helps only as much as it has to.
exercises.note: Reduce the help over the stage: hand on the wrist, then fingers on the wrist, then fingertips only. Add a rep only when the last rep is as clean as the first. Stop at any elbow pain.

exercises.name: One-arm hang
exercises.cue: The other hand takes some weight (on the wrist or a band) if the shoulder complains. Stop at any elbow pain.

stages.name: One-arm negatives
stages.work: 6–8 s lowering, ≤ 4 reps per arm per session

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
exercises.cue: Arms straight. Pull the shoulder blades down; the elbows do not bend.

exercises.name: Assisted one-arm pull-up
exercises.cue: Pull with one arm. Fingertips on the working wrist, no more help than that.
exercises.note: This is a warm-up for the negatives. Use a little more help if the form slips.

exercises.name: One-arm negative
exercises.cue: Chin over the bar to start, then lower with one arm in one slow, steady motion.
exercises.note: Pull up with both hands or jump to the top, let one hand go, then lower. No more than 4 reps per arm in a session. Start at 6 s and stretch toward 8 s. If you cannot control the lowering, stop and rest. Stop at any elbow pain.

exercises.name: One-arm hang
exercises.cue: The other hand takes some weight (on the wrist or a band) if the shoulder complains. Stop at any elbow pain.

stages.name: One-arm pull-up
stages.work: Partials from 90° to the top, then full attempts

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
exercises.cue: Arms straight. Pull the shoulder blades down; the elbows do not bend.

exercises.name: One-arm hang
exercises.cue: The other hand takes some weight (on the wrist or a band) if the shoulder complains. Stop at any elbow pain.

exercises.name: One-arm partial, from 90°
exercises.cue: Elbow bent at 90°, other hand off the bar, then pull until the chin is over.
exercises.note: Stand on a step to set up the 90° start. Once these feel solid, start a little lower each week until you start from a full hang. Stop at any elbow pain.

exercises.name: Full one-arm pull-up attempt
exercises.cue: Hang fully, no swing, no kick, chin over the bar.
exercises.note: Strict means a full hang at the bottom and the chin clearly over the bar. Heavy days only: on a light day, stop after the partials. Rest fully between attempts and stop early if the elbow aches.
